content: <thought>Analyzing the mass spectrum, the most distinctive isotopic pattern is a +2 Da peak (m/z 235.9606) with an intensity of ~24 % relative to the monoisotopic peak (m/z 233.9632). This matches the natural abundance ratio of chlorine (^35Cl/^37Cl ≈ 3:1), which gives a +2 Da peak at about 24 % of the base peak when a single chlorine atom is present. No other element shows a characteristic isotopic pattern (e.g., bromine would give a 1:1 +2 Da peak, sulfur a much smaller ~4 % peak). Therefore, chlorine is the only element that can be definitively identified from the observed isotopic distribution.
